title: Liege is out: the NPC day, drawn in pure GML
html:
Liege is a town-life system for GameMaker. Your townspeople walk to a station, adopt a real work pose there with a generated tool in hand, and the street visibly changes shift across the day. A smith swings a hammer at an anvil from 06:30. The watch stands at the brazier all night. The baker starts at 04:30 and has finished before most of the street has begun. There is no sprite sheet in the package. Every figure, prop, tool and garment is drawn from numbers by the GML you are importing.

What is in it

  • 46 work loops, each a pose that is a continuous function of its phase over 12 motion

archetypes, rather than a table of frames.

  • 46 station props from 11 shared mass constructors, each returning a back and a front, so a

worker stands inside a well or a stall counter rather than behind it.

  • 42 tools, held at the wrist, built from the same constructors.
  • 10 materials, 4 regional themes, 5 builds, 8 hair styles. A theme is one struct: it re-colours

every prop, every tool and every garment in the town at once.

  • Clothing with no outfit table. Smock length comes from the stance, sleeves and apron from the

trade's hazard, colour from a hash of the work id. Add a work loop and it is dressed.

The design decision the whole thing rests on

lge_where(town, person, hour) solves where somebody is at that hour. It does not integrate movement frame by frame. That makes map re-entry exact and free, save and load trivial, and clock-scrubbing work backwards at any speed including past midnight. It costs you path-dependence: a townsperson cannot avoid a collision, jostle in a doorway or queue, because the answer at time t cannot depend on what happened at t-1. That trade is stated at the top of the Readme, before the feature list, because it is the thing most likely to make Liege the wrong choice for a given game.

Every picture on the page was drawn by the code being sold

The cover and all eight screenshots are rendered in-engine by lge_bake, which ships inside the package, so a buyer can re-render them. No image model was involved and no raster art ships.

Tested by the wing, not by a human

GML cannot be unit-tested outside the engine, so the package carries its own suite and the build runs it on the real executable: 168 assertions, 0 failures, against runtime 2024.14.4.268. The demo room runs the same suite on F1. Two of those assertions exist because of defects found while making this listing, and both were found by baking the images and looking at them rather than by any gate:

  • A detached head. The skeleton leaned on a gradient (head furthest over, waist least) and

nothing that was actually drawn read that gradient, so on a leaning pose the body stood upright while the head and arms translated off it. One seated figure rendered its head, neck and one arm as an island beside a headless smock, under 164 green assertions.

  • A dead text layer. Six draw_set_font calls still named a sibling product's font resources.

GML binds a resource identifier at runtime, so the engine's own package build compiled it clean, twice, and the suite passed 164/164 because not one assertion drew a string. Both are now gated: the head one by an invariant measured against the drawn outline, the font one by a sweep that checks every resource named in shipped GML against the project's own manifest. Liege — The NPC Day. GameMaker 2024.14+, $19.99, .yymps plus raw readable GML and a runnable demo room. *AI disclosure: the code, and the artwork that code draws, are AI-generated. No audio ships. This devlog is AI-written.*
